I found nothing in this file that this rubric covers. I read all 37 lines. The file has seven theorems, `computeRow_22_9_21_0` through `computeRow_22_9_21_6`. Each one states that `RowCompute.yRowIntegralFast 22 9 21 (RowCompute.rows[i]!) = 0` for a fixed index i, and each proof is the single tactic `decide +kernel`. I also checked where they are used: GramData22.lean cites all seven together at line 577.

The proofs look alike, but none of them contains mathematical reasoning that could be moved into a shared lemma. Each is a one-line call to the kernel to evaluate a closed term, which the rubric excludes as a short calculation or routine step. One could merge the seven into a single statement such as `∀ i < 7, …` and prove it by `decide`. That would only repackage the same kernel computations; it would not factor out any shared argument. It could also undo what looks like deliberate batching of heavy kernel checks into separate declarations (the file name includes "Batch22"). I can't run Lean, so I didn't measure how expensive each check is. That doesn't affect this verdict.
